question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, the distribution of $Y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Y=4{X}_{1}-2{X}_{2} & ∼N(4{\mu }_{1}-2{\mu }_{2},16{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+4{\sigma }_{2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(20-16,48+16) \\  & ∼N(4,64).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =4$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{64}=8.$ 

We want to find $P(Y<14).$ Thus, we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<14) & =P(Z<\frac{14-4}{8}) \\  & =P(Z<1.25) \\  & =Φ(1.25)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(1.25)≈0.8944.
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(Y<14)≈0.89.
$$
